items.title: U of Arizona climbs in global rankings for earth and water sciences
items.subtitle: Higher scores boost reputation and attract research funding for students.
items.detail: The University of Arizona’s earth and water sciences departments have jumped higher in worldwide rankings. Better scores mean the school’s reputation improves, attracting more research grants and top faculty. For students, this translates into more funding opportunities, cutting‑edge projects, and stronger resumes. Keep an eye on new research initiatives and scholarship announcements that often follow a ranking boost.

items.title: NSF CAREER Award fuels breakthrough battery research at USC
items.subtitle: Students gain access to cutting‑edge labs and industry partnerships.
items.detail: A professor at USC just earned an NSF CAREER Award to develop next‑generation batteries. The grant brings state‑of‑the‑art labs and partnerships with industry leaders directly to campus. Students in engineering and chemistry can now join advanced experiments, internships, and co‑op programs tied to the research. Watch for upcoming lab rotations and project listings that will open soon.

items.title: DHS appeals judge's block on ‘duration of status’ rule for international students
items.subtitle: Potential changes could shorten stay limits for many overseas scholars.
items.imageQuery: court gavel, immigration office, student passport
items.detail: The Department of Homeland Security is appealing a court order that stopped the new “duration of status” rule, which would let schools set shorter time limits for international students to stay after graduation. If the rule returns, many students could face tighter deadlines for work visas or further study. Stay informed through your school’s international office and be ready to adjust plans if the rule is reinstated.

items.title: Australia tightens student visa rules to curb ‘visa hopping’
items.subtitle: New restrictions affect course changes and work rights for incoming students.
items.imageQuery: australian flag, airport arrivals, visa document
items.detail: Australia has tightened its student visa policy to stop “visa hopping,” meaning students can’t easily switch courses or jobs to extend their stay. The changes limit how often you can change programs and reduce work‑hour allowances. If you’re planning to study there, check the new criteria early, choose a program you’re confident about, and talk to your prospective university’s visa adviser about compliance.

items.title: Michigan State expands free tuition program for eligible undergraduates
items.subtitle: More students can graduate debt‑free with the broadened eligibility.
items.imageQuery: college graduation, tuition waiver banner, students cheering
items.detail: Michigan State University broadened its free‑tuition program, now covering more undergraduate majors and income levels. More students can graduate without taking on debt, especially those in high‑cost fields. Eligible students should re‑apply through the financial‑aid portal, and advisors recommend reviewing the updated eligibility checklist to secure the benefit for the upcoming semester.

items.title: California's new housing laws aim to ease student dorm shortages
items.subtitle: Four statutes could unlock more affordable on‑campus living options.
items.imageQuery: college dormitory, construction crane, student moving boxes
items.detail: California passed four housing bills aimed at easing the chronic shortage of student dorms. The laws encourage universities to build more affordable on‑campus housing and streamline approval processes. This could mean lower rent and more options for students next year. Watch campus housing announcements and consider applying early for any new residence halls that open.

items.title: Study in the USA Without SAT: Top test‑optional schools for 2027‑28
items.subtitle: International applicants can apply to these universities without standardized scores.
items.imageQuery: college brochure, international flag, laptop application form
items.detail: A new list of test‑optional colleges for 2027‑28 lets international applicants apply without SAT or ACT scores. Schools are focusing on holistic reviews, valuing essays, grades, and extracurriculars instead. If you’re applying, strengthen your personal statement and showcase projects or leadership roles. Keep track of each school’s specific deadline and any supplemental materials they request.

items.title: University of Delaware sued over in‑state tuition for non‑citizens
items.subtitle: Legal battle may reshape tuition policies for undocumented students nationwide.
items.imageQuery: court building, university sign, protest signs
items.detail: The University of Delaware faces a lawsuit over its policy that offers in‑state tuition to undocumented students. A court ruling could force colleges nationwide to change how they set tuition rates for non‑citizens. Students affected should monitor the case’s progress and consult their school’s legal aid office for guidance on tuition and enrollment options.

items.title: LANL Foundation opens applications for four‑year scholarships
items.subtitle: Funding covers tuition, research travel, and living costs for STEM majors.
items.imageQuery: scholarship award ceremony, lab coat, grant check
items.detail: The Los Alamos National Laboratory Foundation is now accepting applications for four‑year scholarships that cover tuition, research travel, and living expenses for STEM majors. Recipients will join a network of scholars and gain mentorship from top scientists. Start preparing your research proposal and transcripts now; applications typically close in early winter.

items.title: Ball State secures $150,000 for nursing student scholarships
items.subtitle: Financial aid targets the growing demand for qualified nursing professionals.
items.detail: Ball State University received a $150,000 grant to fund scholarships for nursing students, addressing the growing need for qualified nurses. The awards will reduce tuition costs and may include clinical placement support. Interested nursing majors should check the scholarship portal for eligibility criteria and application deadlines, which are usually announced each spring.
